title: Rollout safeguard strip for batching & cache policy diffs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Engineering teams currently change batching and prefix/KV cache policies via the Performance -> Batching & Cache page, then separately configure rollouts. We frequently see rollouts fail because cache/batching changes shift latency/cost distributions in ways that invalidate SLO assumptions. Problem: there is no compact, explainable preview in the deploy flow showing the expected operational impact of a config change across canary/percentage-based rollouts. Proposal: Add a "Rollout safeguard strip" in the Deploy / Rollout review step that surfaces a compact diff summary for batching & cache policy changes. The strip should present estimated delta on p95 latency, per-token cost, cache hit rate, top affected routes, and a data-driven risk band with suggested canary parameters and automatic rollback triggers.
goals: Make it easy for engineers and PMs to see the operational impact of batching/cache changes before rollout
Reduce post-rollout incidents caused by unintended latency/cost shifts
Offer clear, actionable guardrail suggestions (canary %, duration, rollback triggers) based on traffic profiles
Keep the UI compact so it fits inline with existing rollout review flows and mobile widths
non_goals: Replacing the entire Batching & Cache policy editor (this is a rollout-stage summary only)
Making exact predictions for absolute latency in new hardware setups (we use relative deltas)
Auto-enforcing policies without explicit user opt-in
proposal_summary: A horizontal, dismissible strip shown above the rollout confirmation button that shows: 1) concise metric deltas (p95 latency +/-, per-token cost +/-, cache hit rate +/-), 2) risk band (Low/Medium/High) with short rationale, 3) suggested canary config (percent, duration) and auto-rollback conditions, 4) one-click 'preview sample requests' to inspect affected examples and cache miss reasons.
design_notes: Visual hierarchy: metric deltas use micro-spark bars + colored +/- pills; risk band uses a simple tri-color chip and an info tooltip that expands to a short explanation
Accessibility: ensure ARIA labels for risk chip and that the strip is keyboard-focusable; colorblind-friendly palette
Compact mode: collapsed view shows only risk chip + overall cost delta; expanded view (chevron) reveals details and sample request preview
Data backfill: if historical traffic is insufficient, show an 'insufficient data' state with conservative suggestions and a link to run a short live-simulate job
acceptance_criteria: Strip appears in the Deploy -> Review step whenever batching or cache policy changes are included in the rollout
Strip shows p50/p95 latency delta, estimated per-token cost delta, cache hit rate delta and top-3 affected routes
Risk band is computed and displayed with a one-line rationale and matches backend's risk score mapping
Suggested canary defaults populate the rollout form when accepted by the user
One-click "Preview sample requests" opens an inline panel listing up to 10 representative requests and highlights predicted cache misses and prefix mismatches
Collapsed/expanded states function and keyboard navigation works per accessibility guidelines
If historical data is insufficient, the strip displays a clear 'insufficient data' indicator and a CTA to run a live simulation
prototype_notes: Prototype includes animated expand/collapse and the sample request hover inspector
Microcopy for the risk rationale uses short sentences with links to 'why we think this' that open the model used for risk estimation
We experimented with both numeric risk scores and categorical bands; the team prefers categorical bands for quick recognition
implementation_timeline: Week 1: Design handoff and final mocks
Week 2: Frontend + API contract work (risk score + sample-request API)
Week 4: Canary and monitoring, small internal beta
dependencies_notes: Requires ENG work to produce a per-change risk score API and a lightweight sample-request query endpoint. Also depends on PM prioritizing rollout form changes and a short analytics job to compute delta estimates from recent traffic profiles.

Design will handle the UX variations for 'insufficient_data' and collapsed/expanded states.
